speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any unintentional weight loss or changes in your bowel habits? Also, how long have you noticed the increase in your abdominal girth?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the shortness of breath and large ovarian mass, are you experiencing any chest pain or palpitations, and have you noticed any abdominal pain or early satiety? I would like to proceed with imaging to assess the extent of the disease. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan was normal, let's look closer at the chest symptoms. Have you experienced any coughing up blood, night sweats, or a persistent dry cough? I would like to order a Chest X-Ray to investigate the shortness of breath further. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the large ovarian mass and right-sided pleural effusion, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles? I would like to evaluate for ascites and request an ultrasound of the abdomen. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a large ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion is highly suggestive of Meigs syndrome. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out ovarian cancer, I need to assess the mass characteristics further. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of fibroids or other benign gynecological conditions, and have you noticed any tenderness in the abdominal mass upon examination? I need to distinguish between a benign fibrothecoma and a malignant ovarian tumor.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: To confirm Meigs syndrome, I need to rule out malignancy by checking tumor markers. REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CA-125, along with the triad of ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion, strongly confirms Meigs syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs syndrome
